faces.title: As a Consultant
faces.text: Nearly 20 years, 125+ corporate clients, thousands of individual clients. I've seen the harshest side of the workplace and the most beautiful transformations. If you're at a career crossroads, I might help you see the way.

faces.title: As an HR Executive
faces.text: Since 2016, I've been the #1 HR at listed foreign companies, private enterprises, and startups. Interviewed tens of thousands, laid off thousands, and personally orchestrated organizational transformation, talent strategy, cultural重塑, and efficiency improvement. JV, MNC, private, startup — I've immersed in every organizational ecosystem. These experiences help me understand both organizational logic and individual struggles.

faces.title: As a Practicing Lay Buddhist
faces.text: Seek truth through illusions is not about escaping the mundane, but living authentically within each role. Precepts are not bondage but freedom — work is my dojo, relationships are my mirror, cultivating a clear mind amid worldly affairs.

faces.title: As a Vegetarian Lifestyle Advocate
faces.text: 13 years vegetarian — not restraint, but choice. The body is a vessel for practice; every meal is reverence for life. I believe how you treat food reflects how you treat yourself.

faces.title: As a Content Creator
faces.text: Not just writing articles — themed videos, music works, audio podcasts. Each creative form is another practice of truth. Output is not the goal; shared cultivation is.

faces.title: As a Tech Practitioner
faces.text: I vibe code, deploy AI applications, and do deep data analysis. Technology is not the end — serving human growth is. I believe the best consultant will be the one armed with AI.

faces.title: As a Project Management Expert
faces.text: PMP certified, managing every consulting project with PM thinking. From diagnosis to delivery — not just an idea, but a traceable path.

faces.title: As a Life Care Volunteer
faces.text: Life care is not charity — it's seeing. Through health education and hospice volunteering, I deeply understand the wisdom of 'prevention before illness.' The deepest compassion is teaching people to live well before illness arrives. Giving brings you closer to freedom than taking — this is the deepest lesson I've learned.

faces.title: As a Bilingual National Tour Guide
faces.text: A bilingual tour guide license — not a career backup, but opening the world through another language. Every tour is a cross-cultural shared practice.

faces.title: As a Licensed High School Chinese Teacher
faces.text: A high school Chinese teaching credential — not a career alternative, but a deep affection for my mother tongue and reverence for classical studies. Language is the foundation of culture; teaching is the best form of learning, and classics are forever the best teachers.

faces.title: Still Exploring
faces.text: 'I' is just an illusory construct, growing as sentient beings need me to master new skills. More slashes may be unlocked ahead — not because of lack, but because the world is vast and worth staying curious. Exploration itself is the answer.

philosophy.heroSub: Minimal Material · Maximal Capability · Supreme Spirit
philosophy.heroText: Not chicken soup — a recipe lived out
philosophy.sectionStagesSub: From awareness to awakening, a verifiable path
philosophy.ctaText: Want to see how these ideas become services?

coreIdeology.title: Minimal Material
coreIdeology.desc: Not ascetic restraint, but active choice. 13 years vegetarian, simple living — subtract excess desire to hear your true voice. Less in matter, more in life.

coreIdeology.title: Maximal Capability
coreIdeology.desc: 20 years across 6 industries, from trainer to Group HRD, from client-side to consultant, from HRD to Vibe Coding — always learning, always practicing. Capability is the only asset that will never betray you.

coreIdeology.title: Supreme Spirit
coreIdeology.desc: Seek truth through illusions, live toward death. Work is your dojo, relationships are your mirror, every role is practice. Supreme spirit is not transcending the mundane — it's living authentically within it.

stages.title: See Yourself
stages.desc: The starting point of all change is seeing. Seeing your patterns, beliefs, blind spots. Not judgment, but awareness.

stages.title: Personalize
stages.desc: No one-size-fits-all method. Adapt to context, tailor to the person — let every solution grow in the client's own soil.

stages.title: Live Actively
stages.desc: Not perfection in every area, but holding the foundation of work and family. Turn physical, intellectual, and creative interests into daily practice — exercise the body, feed the mind, express the soul.

stages.title: Awaken
stages.desc: Wake up from NPC to player — no longer passively executing a script, but seeing the game rules and reclaiming choice. Work is not about climbing, but refining the heart through events. Life, aging, illness, death — not fear, but inevitable stages.

methodologies.title: Context-Based Thinking
methodologies.desc: Four decision questions: Whose problem is this? What situation are they in? What is their core need? What solution can grow in this context?
methodologies.desc2: Bodhisattvas fear causes, ordinary people fear results — true masters focus on causes, not outcomes. Instead of worrying about layoffs, ask: what causes can I plant today?
methodologies.example: Facing layoffs: don't start with compensation — ask — what life stage is this person in? What do they fear most? What transition path works best for them?

methodologies.title: Practice Truth Through Roles
methodologies.desc: Cultivate your true inner self through every temporarily played role. Work is the dojo,烦恼 is bodhi — how to observe your mind's fluctuations through each arising frustration, that is the real practice.
methodologies.example: 5000+ layoff experiences: every difficult conversation is an opportunity to cultivate compassion. The layoff is 'illusion'; the empathy cultivated is 'truth'.

methodologies.title: Organizational Quadrant
methodologies.desc: Efficiency × Culture: two dimensions, four quadrants — high efficiency/high culture (thriving), high efficiency/low culture (mechanical), low efficiency/high culture (coasting), low efficiency/low culture (zombie).
methodologies.example: A mid-to-high-end hotel cluster: efficiency met target but culture was fractured → repair cultural bonds first, then restructure, avoiding hard landing.

methodologies.title: Soul Questions
methodologies.desc: What is your true inner vision? What kind of person do you want to become? How satisfied are you with yourself right now? If you had one year left, how would you live? Step deeper to reach your authentic self.
methodologies.example: A 40-year-old executive broke down when asked 'if you had one year left' — he had been living for others' expectations, never asking what he truly wanted.

quotes.text: Work is not asceticism, but it can be a dojo.
Layoffs are an organization's metabolism, but every person metabolized deserves to be seen.
True freedom is not doing whatever you want — it's still being yourself in every role you must play.
Wealth is a lesson, not an answer. What you cultivate is your relationship with desire.
Practice through every role is not escaping the mundane — it's finding the path to truth within it.
There is no one-size-fits-all method, only context-based wisdom.
Management's greatest arrogance is judging others' problems from your own situation.
Consulting is not giving answers — it's helping others grow their own.
Adapting to context doesn't mean no principles — it's principles expressed flexibly in specific situations.
Every organization's illness is known only to its own body.
Awakening is not leaving the world — it's no longer getting lost within it.
Precepts are not bondage — they draw a safe boundary for freedom.
The body is the vessel of practice. Mistreat it and you lose the right to practice.
Life's organization is not about throwing away — it's seeing clearly what's worth keeping.
Living toward death is not pessimism — it's the ultimate clarity.

services.storyP1: 5000 is not a cold number. It's 5000 late-night calls, 5000 difficult conversations, 5000 turning points in people's lives. Behind every number is a specific face, a family, a life going through its storm.
services.storyP2: At its core, working for a company is a win-win balance between organization and individual — you contribute ability and time, the company provides platform and return. But when business pivots, strategy shifts, or your own value proposition changes, this balance breaks. Whether you jump or are pushed, it's the same: balance is lost, time to choose again.
services.storyP3: I've seen a post-95 employee win the excellence award in the afternoon and get laid off that evening — not because she wasn't good enough, but because the business line was cut. I've seen an 18-year veteran HR draft her own departure agreement and sit in her car for two hours. I've also seen middle-aged people who felt relieved after being laid off: 'I've wanted to leave for a long time, I just never had the courage.'
services.storyP4: What I can do is not choose between 'cold' and 'warm' — because this work is inherently contradictory. What I strive for is: let those leaving leave with dignity, let those staying not live in fear, so that every time the balance breaks, both sides can turn around gracefully.
